Pi chanai 屬泰國 pi 家族四簧管樂器；pi 為泰國皮帕特（pipha: The pi chanai belongs to the Thai pi family of quadruple-reed wind instruments; the pi is used in the Thai piphat traditional ensemble. The pi chanai is a two-part reed pipe (pi song thon), made of a wooden or ivory body (lao pi) and a bell (lamphong). The source suggests its music came from India, since it resembles the Indian shehnai; the pi has been used in Thailand since the Sukhothai period. The modern pi chanai is often played with the pi chawa (Javanese pi) in processions and concerts, which the Chinese source also calls parade music. Its construction and playing technique resemble the Burmese hne and the Cambodian sralai.

嗩吶音色高亢明亮，具有強烈的穿透力和戲劇性表現力。其音質帶有銅管樂器般的金屬光澤: The suona has a high, bright timbre with strong carrying power and dramatic presence. Its tone has the metallic sheen of a brass instrument together with the warmth of a woodwind. Its range is wide, from a thick, full low register to a piercing high one, spanning more than three octaves. The suona's resonance comes mainly from the vibration of the double reed working with the conical tube, producing rich overtones. Against the saxophone it sounds older and more sinewy; against the trumpet it has more of a vernacular character and a weathered feel. In an ensemble the suona often takes the solo or leading role; it is loud and easily stands out, and is highly recognisable and affecting.
